exchange.text:
**Takeaway:** NVDA leads decisively on profitability and growth, AAPL is the largest by absolute revenue but growing slowly, and AMD sits last on both margins and scale. The three companies occupy very different positions in the hardware stack, and the data reflects that.

**Trend across periods shown:** Only one fiscal year per company is displayed, so there is no multi-period trend to trace. The revenue growth rates give a snapshot of momentum: NVDA is growing fastest, AMD second, and AAPL slowest.

**What is strong and what is weak:** NVDA's gross margin of 70.8% and net margin of 53.6% for FY2026 (ended January 2026) are the highest of the three, and NVDA's revenue growth of 60.9% is also the highest. AAPL's revenue of $416.2B for FY2025 (ended September 2025) is the largest, but AAPL's revenue growth of 6.4% is the lowest. AMD's net margin of 12.0% for FY2025 (ended December 2025) is the lowest, and AMD's revenue of $34.7B is the smallest. Note that the fiscal years end up to four months apart, so these are not perfectly aligned periods.

**Counterpoint:** AMD's gross margin of 49.9% is only modestly below AAPL's 46.9%—actually higher—yet AMD's net margin of 12.0% is far below AAPL's 26.9%. This gap between gross and net margin suggests AMD's operating cost structure is materially heavier relative to revenue. A management statement published in August 2025 attributes approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges to U.S. export controls on AMD Instinct MI308 data center GPU products in the quarter ending around June 2025, which would have pressured that fiscal year's results.

**What the data cannot tell:** No prior-year revenue, gross margin, or net margin is shown for any of the three companies, so we cannot see whether margins are expanding or compressing. No segment or product-line breakdown is provided, so we cannot tell how much of NVDA's margin advantage comes from data-center versus other segments. No operating margin is shown, which would help explain the gap between gross and net margin at AMD.
